sector: Rural Asset Management / Financial Services (NZ Agri)
overview: Allied Farmers is the surviving remnant of a 2009-era NZ finance-company collapse (it absorbed Hanover Finance and United Finance's loan books) that has spent 15+ years rebuilding into a small-cap rural investment and asset-management company with a large ($172m) unrecognised tax loss pool. Following the 1 December 2025 sale of its 67.8%-owned livestock agency NZ Farmers Livestock (NZFL) to Rural Livestock Limited, Allied is now a pure-play rural asset manager: its core asset is 100% ownership of New Zealand Rural Land Management (NZRLM), the external manager of NZX-listed farmland REIT New Zealand Rural Land Company (NZL), alongside a parent-level investment portfolio (a ~2.75% NZL shareholding, a $10.5m Waikato investment property, and a $3m secured farm loan). It operates entirely within New Zealand and is listed on the NZX Main Board (ALF). The NZFL sale consideration has now been fully finalised as of June 2026 (final adjustment statement agreed and settled), leaving only a small $0.5m tax-loss-offset payment due April 2027.

business_model.summary: Allied now earns recurring, asset-based management, transaction and performance fees from NZRLM's contract to manage NZL's farmland portfolio, supplemented by parent-level investment income (rent, interest, dividends) and the run-off of a large legacy tax-loss pool that shelters future profits from tax. The FY2025-vintage livestock agency/finance business (NZFL) that historically drove ~85% of consolidated revenue has been divested and is now shown as a discontinued operation; H1 FY2026 was the first period reported on a pure continuing-operations (asset management) basis, and FY2026 full-year results (due on or before 29 August 2026) will be the first clean annual read on this business, containing only five months of legacy NZFL trading.

revenue_streams.name: NZ Farmers Livestock (livestock agency, veal export, finance) - DIVESTED Dec-2025, sale proceeds fully settled Jun-2026

business_model.customer_type: B2B/institutional - single major counterparty (NZL, an NZX-listed REIT) for management fees; farm-loan borrower and property tenant relationships at parent level

main_competitors: Colliers/Bayleys rural real estate & farm management teams
Rural Livestock Limited (livestock agency, now owns former NZFL business)
Direct farmland ownership/syndicates as an alternative to NZL
competitive_position.market_position: Niche, single-mandate external manager of one NZX-listed farmland vehicle (NZL); very small market capitalisation (micro-cap) with limited scale versus diversified rural services players

moat_factors.description: NZRLM holds the management contract for NZL, a listed structure with switching costs and governance friction, but the contract itself is not perpetual/guaranteed and NZL could in theory internalise management or replace the manager. NZL's Jan-2024 sale of 25% of its land portfolio to Roc Partners (via a limited partnership structure) added a co-investor with its own governance interest in NZRLM's mandate, though no change to the management arrangement has been disclosed

Managing Director Richard Milsom co-founded NZRLM/NZL and holds ~15.8% of Allied; WAF Limited (a friendly ~20% holder) provides stable, aligned ownership reducing takeover/activist risk. NZL co-founder and long-serving director Christopher Swasbrook resigned from NZL's board effective 30 April 2026 (no reason given); NZL also ran a board performance/composition review with Propero Consulting through H1 2026 (outcome not yet publicly disclosed as of Aug-2026). Both are governance changes at the client entity worth monitoring but not indicative of any mandate issue disclosed to date

A substantial legacy tax-loss pool shelters future profits from tax, provided shareholder continuity thresholds are maintained - a real economic asset unusual for a company this size, and a stated capital-allocation driver (Allied prioritises growth investments that can use the losses over dividends)

moat_factors.factor: Niche expertise in NZ farmland/agri asset management
moat_factors.description: Specialist knowledge of NZ pastoral, horticultural and forestry land valuation and management built over years running NZL's farmland portfolio (~17,400+ha as at mid-2026, following continued bolt-on acquisitions including a Central Otago orchard property completed July 2026 and a dairy farm purchase from an existing tenant)

weaknesses: Single-client revenue concentration - NZRLM's fee income depends almost entirely on the size, performance and continued existence of one external entity, NZL
Very small scale and float - illiquid micro-cap stock with concentrated register (WAF 19.99%, Rem Trustee 12.45%, Milsom 15.8%) limiting institutional interest

No pricing power over management fee terms, which are set by a negotiated management agreement with NZL and can be reviewed/renegotiated (evidenced by NZL's Jan/Feb-2026 KPMG capital review, which concluded without any change to the NZRLM management arrangement but reset NZL's own dividend/capital policy)
History of destroyed shareholder capital during the 2009-2012 finance-company collapse continues to weigh on market perception/valuation

Post-NZFL-sale earnings base is small and volatile, with H1 FY2026 continuing operations posting a pre-tax loss, and management has guided full FY2026 group results will be significantly lower than prior years

growth_drivers: Growth in NZL's farmland AUM (acquisitions, portfolio revaluation) directly grows NZRLM's base and performance fees - NZL continued to add to its portfolio in 2026 (Central Otago SI Orchards property completed July 2026; a dairy farm acquired from an existing tenant), evidencing continued deployment despite the Jan-2024 Roc Partners partial sell-down

NZL's Jan/Feb-2026 'YieldPlusGrowth' capital management framework (post-KPMG review) targets AFFO-per-share-accretive growth and a formalised dividend policy (quarterly, ~90-100% of AFFO; NZL FY25 AFFO 5.43cps, +9.9% YoY, FY26 guided to 5.65-5.99cps), which could expand NZL's capital base, investor appeal and Allied's fee pool over time

NZFL sale consideration now fully finalised: Allied's total take is $5.814m (received H1 FY2026) plus a further $2.40m received by June 2026 on final working-capital/adjustment settlement, with only a residual $0.5m tax-loss-offset payment due April 2027 - clean cash to redeploy
Redeployment of NZFL sale proceeds plus existing cash (~$10.8m at Dec-2025, since augmented by the $2.40m June-2026 receipt) into new rural investments that can utilise the $172m tax-loss pool
Simplified, focused strategy as a pure asset manager/investor may re-rate the stock versus its prior diversified/lower-margin livestock trading business
Potential for NZRLM to win additional mandates or expand services beyond NZL over time

Rising NZ interest rates (RBNZ resumed hiking July 2026, OCR to 2.50%, further hikes flagged for Sept/Oct 2026 toward ~3%) increase interest income earned on Allied's large cash balance, partially offsetting higher cost of debt on the Heartland/MC Redlands facilities

business.description: Virtually all continuing-operations fee income comes from the NZRLM/NZL management agreement; loss, renegotiation, or underperformance of NZL would materially impair Allied's earnings

business.risk: Small, volatile earnings base post-NZFL divestment
business.description: H1 FY2026 continuing operations posted a pre-tax loss of $0.517m; the company is still bedding down its new operating model and cost base; Allied has flagged that full-year FY2026 financial statements will be significantly lower than prior years given the NZFL sale timing (only five months of legacy NZFL trading included) - the FY2026 annual result, due on or before 29 August 2026 (roughly three weeks from now), is the next test of the standalone earnings power of the continuing business

Strategy depends on management successfully redeploying sale proceeds and cash (now ~$13m+ following the June-2026 final NZFL settlement receipt) into new rural investments/loans that generate adequate risk-adjusted returns; no committed pipeline has been publicly disclosed

financial.risk: Illiquidity of NZL shares and investment property
financial.description: Allied holds ~2.75% of NZL and a $10.5m investment property (via an SPV, MC Redlands-financed) - both are relatively illiquid, fair-value-marked assets

The Waikato property SPV loan (MC Redlands Pty Ltd, $10.5m fair-valued financial liability) is complex and its fair value has already moved materially ($9.568m initial recognition to $10.496m by Jun-2025, $10.500m by Dec-2025)

financial.risk: Residual exposure on NZFL loan book/settlement
financial.description: Allied's continuing-involvement obligation on NZFL's transferred loan book has now been resolved: the final adjustment statement was agreed and Allied's $2.40m additional share received by June 2026, leaving only a $0.5m tax-loss-offset payment due April 2027 as residual exposure

regulatory.risk: Shareholder continuity rules threaten tax loss utilisation
regulatory.description: The $172.4m unrecognised tax loss pool can only be used if NZ shareholder continuity thresholds continue to be met; Allied has already amended its constitution and obtained NZX/NZ RegCo waivers (2024) to restrict share transfers and protect continuity

regulatory.risk: NZX Major Transaction / FMC Act compliance
regulatory.description: Significant transactions (e.g., the NZFL sale) require shareholder approval as Major Transactions under NZX Listing Rule 5.1.1(a), creating execution/timing risk for future portfolio moves

macro.risk: NZ farmland values and agri-commodity cycle
macro.description: NZRLM fee income (especially performance fees) is tied to NZL's net asset value, which moves with NZ farmland valuations, dairy/livestock prices, and farmer confidence

Parent-level and subsidiary borrowings (Heartland Bank facility at BKBM+4%, MC Redlands loan) are sensitive to NZ interest rates; investment property values are also rate-sensitive. RBNZ resumed hiking the OCR in July 2026 (to 2.50%, first hike since May 2023) after a prolonged hold, with further hikes flagged for the 2 September and 28 October 2026 reviews toward ~3% - a reversal of the prior easing bias that raises borrowing costs on Allied's debt and NZL's cost of capital, though it also lifts interest income on Allied's ~$10.8m+ cash balance

macro.risk: US tariffs / geopolitical impact on NZ agri exports
macro.description: Indirect exposure via NZL's farm tenants and broader NZ agri sentiment, though direct livestock/export exposure has been removed with the NZFL sale

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ farmland values and the listed rural-land/asset-management niche remain small but are supported by a cyclical upswing in NZ agri commodity prices (strong 2024/25/26 dairy and livestock pricing) and renewed institutional interest in farmland as an asset class (evidenced by NZL's capital review, move to a formalised dividend-paying 'yield plus growth' model from Jan/Feb-2026 targeting 90-100% of AFFO paid quarterly, and continued bolt-on land acquisitions through mid-2026 including a Central Otago orchard and a dairy farm)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - NZRLM fee income (particularly performance fees) is linked to NZL's NAV and transaction activity, which correlates with the NZ dairy/agri cycle and land values; parent investment income is comparatively stable
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate, now in a rising-rate environment - the RBNZ resumed raising the OCR in July 2026 (to 2.50%, first hike since May 2023) after a prolonged hold/easing cycle, with further hikes expected at the September and October 2026 reviews toward ~3%. This raises the cost of Allied's own borrowings (Heartland facility, MC Redlands property loan) and NZL's cost of capital/land valuations, but also increases interest income on Allied's substantial net-cash position, a partial natural offset for a holdco with more cash than debt
key_input_costs: NZ farmland valuations (drives performance fees, not a direct input cost)

recent_developments.event: Allied Farmers announced a conditional agreement to sell 100% of NZ Farmers Livestock Limited (NZFL) to Rural Livestock Limited for an enterprise value of $10.988m
Shareholders approved the NZFL sale as a Major Transaction at the Annual Meeting (6 Nov 2025)

Sale of NZFL to Rural Livestock Limited completed; NZFL deconsolidated. Allied received $5.814m of its ~67.77% share of proceeds in H1 FY2026, and retained continuing involvement/exposure in NZFL's residual loan book, recognising a $1.932m continuing involvement obligation and $2.745m of related receivables at 31 Dec 2025

NZL (the entity NZRLM manages) completed an independent KPMG capital review (announced 28 Jan 2026), concluding NZL is valued primarily on cash-yield sustainability; adopted a new 'YieldPlusGrowth' capital management framework targeting quarterly distributions of ~90-100% of AFFO and AFFO-per-share-accretive growth/buyback decisions. NZL's FY25 (Dec-2025 year-end) result showed NPAT $7.9m (down from $17.4m in FY24, driven by non-cash fair-value/derivative items) on revenue of $22.3m (+12% YoY), and AFFO of 5.43cps (+9.9% YoY), a 90.5% payout (4.91cps), with FY26 AFFO guidance of 5.65-5.99cps

H1 FY2026 (six months to 31 Dec 2025) results: consolidated profit after tax of $3.542m (+44.8% YoY), driven by the NZFL sale gain ($2.110m) and a $2.740m income tax benefit; continuing operations (post-NZFL, i.e. the ongoing asset-management business) posted a pre-tax LOSS of $0.517m due to NZFL sale transaction costs and higher NZRLM operating/transaction costs; NTA per share rose to $0.70 (from $0.50/$0.54 attributable/consolidated at Jun-2025); no interim dividend declared. Allied also flagged full FY2026 financial statements will be significantly lower than prior years, reflecting the NZFL sale timing (only five months of legacy NZFL trading in the FY2026 comparatives) and the loss of its former largest revenue line

Christopher Swasbrook, an NZL co-founder and director since Sept-2020, resigned from the NZL board effective 30 April 2026; no reason disclosed. This is a governance change at NZL (Allied's client/managed entity), not at Allied itself, and has not been linked to any change in the NZRLM management mandate

NZL held its Annual Meeting (20 May 2026, virtual) alongside a board composition/performance review with Propero Consulting that commenced in H1 2026; outcome of the review has not been publicly disclosed as of Aug-2026

NZFL sale final adjustment statement agreed and fully settled. Allied received its 67.7% share of an additional $2.40m in adjusted purchase price and other contractual amounts (on top of the $5.814m already received), effectively finalising the transaction. A residual $0.5m payment tied to a tax-loss offset arrangement for the Jul-Dec 2026 period is expected in April 2027. Company explicitly reiterated that because the sale completed 1 Dec 2025, FY2026 financial statements will include only five months of NZFL trading, so FY2026 group revenue and earnings will be materially lower than prior years

NZL (via a limited partnership 75%-owned by NZL) completed the acquisition of the remaining SI Orchards property in Roxburgh East, Central Otago, expanding its horticultural land portfolio; NZL also acquired a dairy farm from an existing tenant post-balance-date, evidencing continued AUM growth under NZRLM's management that underpins Allied's fee base

RBNZ resumed raising the Official Cash Rate for the first time since May 2023, lifting it 25bp to 2.50% at its 8 July 2026 review; markets and economists expect further hikes at the 2 September and 28 October 2026 reviews, potentially toward ~3% - a macro reversal relevant to Allied's net-cash position and its Heartland/MC Redlands borrowings

FY2025 annual report: audited NPAT of $3.841m (FY24: $6.919m, which included a one-off $4.2m Frankton saleyards gain); FY25 profit after tax attributable to Allied shareholders of $2.871m, EPS 9.97cps; NZFL delivered a much-improved result on a buoyant livestock market

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 results (six months to 31 December 2025), released February 2026; NZFL settlement update, June 2026

items.target: No dividends; retain and redeploy earnings
items.notes: Management reiterated its long-standing no-dividend policy, prioritising redeployment of earnings/proceeds into growth investments that can utilise the $172.4m tax-loss pool. No new dividend commitment made since H1 FY2026 results; unchanged as of Aug-2026

items.metric: NZFL loan book continuing-involvement recovery / final settlement
items.target: Full recovery of receivables / final settlement
items.notes: As of June 2026, Allied confirmed the NZFL sale final adjustment statement was agreed and its $2.40m additional share received, effectively closing out the continuing-involvement obligation. Only a residual $0.5m tax-loss-offset payment (covering Jul-Dec 2026) remains outstanding, expected April 2027 - a favourable resolution versus the original May-2026 target, now fully realised in cash terms bar this small tail payment

items.target: NZRLM to achieve NPBT 10% higher than FY25 NPAT (25% weight); strategy/transaction/leadership targets (75% weight)
items.notes: Reflects the shift to a pure NZRLM/asset-management focus following the NZFL divestment; implies management expects NZRLM NPBT growth of at least 10% in FY26

items.target: Significantly lower reported net profit than prior years
items.notes: Management explicitly guided that FY2026 financial statements will be significantly lower than previous years due to the loss of NZFL as a revenue line (only five months of legacy NZFL trading included) and the timing of the divestment gain being recognised in H1 rather than repeating; reiterated again in the June 2026 settlement update. FY2026 annual results are due on or before 29 August 2026 (roughly three weeks away) and will be the first clean full-year read on the pure NZRLM/investment business - this is the single most important near-term catalyst for the stock

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Shelley Ruha and MD Richard Milsom framed the NZFL sale as completing Allied's transformation into a focused rural asset manager and investor, deploying capital and tax losses into opportunities managed via its governance structures and NZRLM asset-management expertise. Management noted the Board 'strongly believes retaining and redeploying earnings into investment opportunities that offer sustainable earnings is in shareholders' best interests,' and highlighted continued positive momentum in NZ farm gate conditions into FY26 (albeit with softening in veal/skin pricing prior to the NZFL sale, and uncertainty from US tariffs on NZ agri exports). The June-2026 confirmation that the NZFL sale is now fully settled (bar a small April-2027 tail payment) removes a source of uncertainty ahead of the FY2026 annual result, due on or before 29 August 2026, which remains the next scheduled disclosure catalyst and will be the first full-year report of the pure NZRLM/investment business. H1-2027 interim results are due on or before 1 March 2027.

bull_case: Simplified, higher-margin business model post-NZFL sale: Allied is now a focused rural asset manager (NZRLM) plus an investment portfolio, removing the lower-margin, working-capital-intensive livestock trading business
Enormous unrecognised tax-loss asset ($172.4m) provides years of tax-free compounding for future earnings, provided shareholder continuity is preserved - a structural advantage most micro-caps lack

NZFL sale proceeds are now fully realised in cash (total ~$8.2m to Allied, settled June 2026 bar a small April-2027 tail payment), giving management a clean, de-risked capital base (~$13m+ cash) to redeploy into new rural investments; net-cash balance sheet (~$17.9m net cash bridge, excluding the ring-fenced MC Redlands property loan) trading at ~0.59x book provides a hard downside floor and optionality

NZL's Jan/Feb-2026 KPMG-driven 'YieldPlusGrowth' framework, formalised ~90-100%-of-AFFO quarterly dividend policy, FY26 AFFO growth guidance (5.65-5.99cps), and continued bolt-on land acquisitions through mid-2026 (Central Otago orchard, dairy farm) point to a growing AUM/fee base for NZRLM

Aligned, concentrated insider/friendly ownership (Milsom 15.8%, WAF 19.99%) reduces takeover overhang and points to management incentives tied to long-term NPAT growth (LTIP tied to 3-year average Group NPAT)
bear_case: This is a net-cash shell trading below book value, not a growth story: post-NZFL the operating business (NZRLM fee income) is small, single-mandate and currently loss-making at the pre-tax level (H1 FY26 continuing operations pre-tax loss of $0.517m), so the investment case rests almost entirely on cash redeployment and the tax-loss asset rather than an existing earnings stream

Single-mandate concentration risk: nearly all continuing-operations revenue now depends on one management contract with NZL; any renegotiation, internalisation, or NZL underperformance would be highly damaging, and governance turnover at NZL (Swasbrook's April-2026 board resignation, the still-undisclosed outcome of the Propero board review) bears watching even though no mandate impact has been disclosed

Management has explicitly guided FY2026 full-year results will be significantly lower than prior years (only five months of legacy NZFL trading); the 29-Aug-2026 annual result is the first real test of standalone earnings power and carries binary catalyst risk over the next ~3 weeks

Illiquid micro-cap (~NZ$17m market cap, thin daily volumes) with a small, concentrated share register, likely commanding a persistent valuation discount and limiting institutional/index interest - the market may continue to apply a steep discount to book (0.59x) even after the cash position is fully clean

No dividends and reliance on management's capital-allocation judgement to redeploy sale proceeds and cash into new rural investments - execution risk with no committed pipeline disclosed as of Aug-2026; rising NZ interest rates (RBNZ hiking since July 2026) raise the opportunity-cost bar for any new deployment

Complex related structures (NZL-linked management fees paid partly in NZL shares/performance fees, fair-valued SPV property financing via a $10.5m MC Redlands term loan) add valuation and disclosure complexity for outside investors
Legacy reputational overhang from the 2009-2012 Hanover/United Finance collapse continues to be part of the company's history and market narrative
